context.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
context.conclusion: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

record.definition: AnalyticNotation fixes the following typed conventions, with each function, space, point and measure supplied by its own statement or local scope. D and fderiv denote the Fréchet derivative over the field specified at each use, defaulting to ℝ; deriv is the corresponding one-variable derivative. The total derivative operators return zero when a derivative does not exist. HasDerivAt relates a one-variable function, its derivative value and its basepoint. ContDiffOn and ContDiffAt express the indicated C-order regularity on a set or at a point; ∞ means all finite orders and ω means analytic. minSmoothness at order 2 is 2 for a field satisfying IsRCLikeNormedField and ω otherwise; IsSymmSndFDerivAt means that the second Fréchet derivative at the specified point is symmetric in its two direction arguments. 𝓝 denotes the neighborhood filter. The support of a function is the set where its value is nonzero, tsupport is the closure of that set, and HasCompactSupport means this closure is compact. ContinuousOn means continuity relative to the indicated set. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function. Integrable means ae strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; IntegrableOn means integrability with respect to the restriction of the specified measure to the specified set. The Bochner integral uses the total library convention; for real integrable functions it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. A set indicator equals its function on that set and zero off it. An ae assertion holds outside a null set for the indicated measure. The extended norm on an ESeminormedAddMonoid is denoted by ‖·‖ₑ; real numbers have finite extended norm. Standard structure names retain their usual mathematical meanings: OpensMeasurableSpace says that open sets are measurable, BorelSpace identifies the measurable structure with the Borel structure, IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts says compact sets have finite measure, and IsAddHaarMeasure means an additive Haar measure. These conventions define notation and assert no application theorem.
V(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) t, for each x,t and k∈Fin m.
L(x,t)=∑_{j∈Fin n} Ssp(j,x,t), the componentwise spatial Laplacian.

dx is canonical Lebesgue volume on Space: the product of the usual real Lebesgue measures in its fixed standard coordinates. It is the original dx on ℝⁿ. Spatial integrals without a displayed measure use dx.
e(x,t)=normSq(V(x,t))+∑_{j∈Fin n} normSq(Psp(j,x,t)). This is |u_t|²+∑_j |∂_{x_j}u|² at positive times, with the Euclidean/Frobenius squares and coefficient 1 on each term.
E(t)=∫_{Space} e(x,t) dx, using the total integral convention until integrability is proved. At positive times when integrable this is the original finite energy integral.

The fields ubar,V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d are C∞ on U for every j∈Fin n. For every x∈Space, t>0, k∈Fin m and j∈Fin n: HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) V(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦V(x,r)_k) A(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j,x,r)_k) W(j,x,t)_k t; fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Psp(j,x,t)_k; fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=W(j,x,t)_k; and fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Ssp(j,x,t)_k. In particular the time derivative of Psp(j) and the spatial j derivative of V coincide. Moreover HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t, with d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_j dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)). record.statement: For every t0>0 there exists a compact C⊆Space such that, writing J=[t0/2,3t0/2] and I=(t0/2,3t0/2), ubar(x,r)=q for all x∉C and r∈J. Every positive-order spacetime derivative of ubar vanishes on Cᶜ×I. In particular V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d vanish there. For every r∈I and j∈Fin n,k∈Fin m, all scalar component spatial sections of V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j), the sections e(·,r),d(·,r), and the products V_k A_k, Psp(j)_k W(j)_k, V_k Ssp(j)_k, V_k Psp(j)_k, W(j)_k Psp(j)_k at time r are continuous, have tsupport contained in C, and are dx-integrable. At time r the dot products dot(V,A), dot(Psp(j),W(j)), dot(V,Ssp(j)), dot(V,Psp(j)) and dot(W(j),Psp(j)), and every finite real linear combination of all the listed scalar sections, are likewise continuous, compactly supported in C and integrable. In particular e(·,t) is dx-integrable for every t>0.

record.statement: For every t0>0 and j∈Fin n, ∫_{Space}dot(Psp(j,x,t0),W(j,x,t0)) dx = −∫_{Space}dot(V(x,t0),Ssp(j,x,t0)) dx. Both dot products are integrable. For each k∈Fin m the scalar products V_k Ssp(j)_k, W(j)_k Psp(j)_k and V_k Psp(j)_k at time t0, including the two directional-derivative products in the integration-by-parts application, are integrable.
record.origin: basis-proof.md:33–38; internal proof of class 3 B014.

record.statement: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.
